cards.name: Zipper
cards.summary: Distort tool mode that turns an object's outline into a row of sharp zigzag teeth, like a zipper or a pinking-shear edge: Amplitude sets how tall the teeth are and Frequency how many there are, Smooth rounds them into scallops / waves, Random varies their height for a ragged edge and Local makes them tallest at the origin and shrink away from it. The distortion stays live (editable or clearable) until the object is converted to curves.
use_for: starburst / price-sticker badge from a circle or rounded box
pinking-shear or torn-ticket edge on a coupon, label or tag
electric, shocked or jittery outline on a comic shape or callout
scalloped seal or wavy frame border (Smooth on)
avoid: body text or detailed logos: every path segment gets teeth, so glyphs turn hairy and unreadable; distort a simple backing shape instead
an exact star or seal with a fixed point count: the Star / Polygon tool gives clean, even geometry
precise die-cut lines: tooth spacing follows the object's segments, so uneven segments give uneven teeth; convert to curves and check the nodes
groups such as the imported SVG plate: not verified whether it distorts a group as one object; apply per object if it refuses
bitmaps: this is a vector-only effect; use a bitmap Distort effect on photos

params.name: OriginX
params.does: horizontal position of the distortion centre, in document units; matters most with Local on

params.name: OriginY
params.does: vertical position of the distortion centre, in document units

params.name: Amplitude
params.does: height of the teeth (long; the harvest gives no range)
params.typical: 10-30 for a crisp serrated edge; 50+ for a spiky starburst

params.name: Frequency
params.does: how many teeth are laid along each segment of the outline (long; the harvest gives no range)
params.typical: 5-15 for badges; 20-40 for a fine pinked edge

params.name: Random
params.does: varies tooth heights randomly for a rough, torn or electric edge
params.typical: false; true for torn paper or a shock outline

params.name: Smooth
params.does: rounds the sharp points into smooth waves / scallops
params.typical: true for scalloped seals and wavy borders

params.name: Local
params.does: teeth are tallest at the origin and fade out with distance from it
params.typical: false; true to concentrate the effect on one area

pairs_with: Drop Shadow on the toothed badge for a sticker look
Contour (outside) around the distorted shape for a seal border
Object > Convert to Curves to bake the teeth before node editing or cutting
cards.scripting: VBA: Set eff = s.CreateZipperDistortion(s.CenterX, s.CenterY, 20, 10, False, False, False) (Shape.CreateZipperDistortion(OriginX, OriginY, Amplitude, Frequency, Random, Smooth, Local) -> Effect; the harvest apply test returned effect_type 7). pywin32: s.CreateZipperDistortion(s.CenterX, s.CenterY, 20, 10, False, False, False). Offsets / origins are in ActiveDocument.Unit (inches for a script unless the document unit was changed; the harvest tests used inches). The demo origin 10.0 / 5.625 assumes the 1920x1080 plate sits 1:1 at 96 px/in from the page origin; pass the shape's CenterX / CenterY in practice. Interactive route: Distort tool (cdr_guid f42edc69-976b-4917-802a-1c4fed6297ef) in Zipper mode.
cards.non_destructive: yes: a live distortion effect on the object (edit it on the property bar or clear it) until Convert to Curves bakes the nodes
cards.cost: light: pure vector, but node count grows with Frequency x segments, so heavy Frequency on text slows redraw

review.changes: removed the invented 0-100 property-bar ranges from Amplitude and Frequency (harvest has type long only)

verified.note: The star's outline is turned into rows of sharp sawtooth teeth along every edge (Amplitude 20, Frequency 10), a pinking-shear edge; Random, Smooth and Local off.

cards.name: Drop Shadow
cards.summary: Interactive drop shadow: adds a live, editable shadow behind a vector or bitmap object, either a flat offset shadow (Type Flat) or a perspective cast shadow anchored to the object's bottom, top, left or right edge, with colour, opacity, feathering (edge softness), feather direction / edge shape and merge mode, plus angle, stretch and fade for perspective shadows. The shadow is rendered as a soft bitmap linked to the object and follows it when the object is moved or edited.
use_for: lift a product cut-out, logo or card off its background
soft shadow under headline type on a poster or thumbnail
perspective cast shadow (Bottom) to stand an object on a floor
button / card elevation in UI mock-ups
avoid: coloured or busy backgrounds where a Normal black shadow greys them out: use Merge Mode Multiply or a dark shade of the background colour; on a very dark background a dark shadow barely reads at all
hard flat shadows for vinyl cutting or screen print: the shadow is a bitmap; use Block Shadow or an offset vector duplicate
a shadow inside the shape: use Inner Shadow
very large Feather on big objects: soft, slow and heavy at export; keep feather modest

a shadow on a live Contour group: it follows the inner base shape, not the contour, so a thick sticker border's shadow is nearly invisible; break the group apart first (Break Apart turns the contour into a plain curve) and put the shadow on the outer curve (plan runs 2026-10-15 (cutout_social.sticker_cutout))

copying or flattening a shadowed object: Shape.Duplicate does not copy a live drop shadow (the duplicate reads Effects.Count 0), the shadow lives in a separate group shape (type 16) that holds the object and its shadow, and Shape.ConvertToBitmapEx on the object alone leaves the shadow out: convert the type 16 group; Shape.FlattenEffects on a shadowed star gave a dull indigo shape with no shadow (plan runs 2026-10-15 (print_prep.flatten_transparency))

a second shadow-type effect on the same object: it replaces the first (an inner shadow followed by a drop shadow kept only the drop shadow); put the second one on a duplicate of the shape (plan runs 2026-10-15 (text_effects.letterpress))

params.name: Type
params.does: flat offset shadow, or a perspective shadow cast from the object's bottom / top / left / right edge
params.typical: 0 (Flat) for lift; 1 (Bottom) for a floor shadow

params.name: Opacity
params.does: shadow opacity, in percent

params.name: Feather
params.does: softness of the shadow edge (0 = hard)

params.name: OffsetX
params.does: horizontal shadow offset in document units (flat shadows)

params.name: OffsetY
params.does: vertical shadow offset in document units; negative moves it down

params.name: Color
params.does: shadow colour; the harvested default is Nothing (pass None from Python) for the app's default colour
params.typical: black, or a dark shade of the background colour

params.name: FeatherType
params.does: how the softness spreads: inside, middle, outside, average, or Gaussian blur

params.name: FeatherEdge
params.does: fall-off curve of the feathered edge

params.name: PerspectiveAngle
params.does: direction of a perspective shadow, in degrees

params.name: PerspectiveStretch
params.does: length of a perspective shadow relative to the object

params.name: Fade
params.does: how much a perspective shadow fades out along its length

params.name: MergeMode
params.does: how the shadow blends with what is below it

pairs_with: Inner Shadow on a neighbouring panel for an inset / raised pair
Zipper-distorted badge + Drop Shadow for a sticker look
Block Shadow instead when a solid vector shadow is needed for print
cards.scripting: VBA: Set eff = s.CreateDropShadow(cdrDropShadowFlat, 75, 12, 0.4, -0.4, CreateRGBColor(0, 0, 0), cdrFeatherGaussianBlur, cdrEdgeLinear, -45, 1, 1, cdrMergeMultiply) (Shape.CreateDropShadow(Type, Opacity, Feather, OffsetX, OffsetY, Color, FeatherType, FeatherEdge, PerspectiveAngle, PerspectiveStretch, Fade, MergeMode) -> Effect; harvest test and audit returned effect_type 5). pywin32: s.CreateDropShadow(0, 75, 12, 0.4, -0.4, app.CreateRGBColor(0, 0, 0), 4, 0, -45.0, 1.0, 1, 9); pass None for Color to keep the default. Offsets / origins are in ActiveDocument.Unit (inches for a script unless the document unit was changed; the harvest tests used inches).
cards.non_destructive: yes: a live shadow effect linked to the object; edit or clear it any time, or break it apart to get a separate bitmap
cards.cost: moderate: the shadow is rendered as a bitmap; big Feather on large objects slows redraw and export

review.changes: Color param: default is Nothing per harvest, not black; Opacity: dropped the unharvested 0-100 range; reworded the dark-background avoid (Multiply does not rescue a dark backdrop)

verified.note: A soft black flat drop shadow at 75 % opacity, feathered 12, sits down-right of the star, making it float above the page.

cards.name: Inner Shadow
cards.summary: Adds a live shadow inside a closed vector shape, cast inward from its edges in the direction of the offset (an offset down-right darkens the top and left inner edges), so the shape looks recessed, cut out or debossed into the page. Controls mirror Drop Shadow (opacity, feather, offset, colour, feather direction / edge, merge mode) plus Depth, whose exact role is not documented in the harvest.
use_for: debossed / letterpress look on a label, logo panel or type
inset buttons, wells and input fields in UI mock-ups
cut-out window or hole effect in a poster shape
adding depth to flat-colour headline type
avoid: open paths (like the plate's zigzag line): it needs a closed vector object
photos and other bitmaps: the harvest lists it for closed vector objects only
light shapes with a Normal merge: the shadow barely reads; use Multiply and a darker colour
a shadow outside the shape: use Drop Shadow
groups such as the imported SVG plate: not verified whether it shades each closed child; apply per object if needed

a Drop Shadow added after an Inner Shadow on the same object: shadow-type effects replace each other and only the drop shadow was kept; put one of them on a duplicate of the shape (plan runs 2026-10-15 (text_effects.letterpress))

params.name: Opacity
params.does: shadow opacity, in percent

params.name: Feather
params.does: softness of the inner shadow edge

params.name: OffsetX
params.does: horizontal shift of the shadow in document units; the shadow gathers on the opposite inner edge

params.name: OffsetY
params.does: vertical shift in document units; negative (down) darkens the top inner edge

params.name: Color
params.does: shadow colour; the harvested default is Nothing (pass None from Python) for the app's default colour
params.typical: black or a dark shade of the fill

params.name: FeatherType
params.does: how the softness spreads

params.name: FeatherEdge
params.does: fall-off curve of the feathered edge

params.name: MergeMode
params.does: how the shadow blends with the shape's fill

params.name: Depth
params.does: not explained by the harvest (default -1.0, probably automatic); leave at the default unless tested

pairs_with: Drop Shadow on surrounding shapes for a raised / sunken contrast
Fountain Transparency on a highlight shape for a bevelled, pressed look
cards.scripting: VBA: Set eff = s.CreateInnerShadow(85, 15, 0.25, -0.25, CreateRGBColor(0, 0, 0), cdrFeatherGaussianBlur, cdrEdgeLinear, cdrMergeMultiply, -1) (Shape.CreateInnerShadow(Opacity, Feather, OffsetX, OffsetY, Color, FeatherType, FeatherEdge, MergeMode, Depth) -> Effect; harvest test and audit returned effect_type 11). pywin32: s.CreateInnerShadow(85, 15, 0.25, -0.25, app.CreateRGBColor(0, 0, 0), 4, 0, 9, -1.0). Offsets / origins are in ActiveDocument.Unit (inches for a script unless the document unit was changed; the harvest tests used inches).
cards.non_destructive: yes: a live shadow effect linked to the shape; edit or clear it any time
cards.cost: moderate: rendered as a bitmap clipped inside the shape

review.changes: Color param: default is Nothing per harvest, not black; Opacity: dropped the unharvested 0-100 range

verified.note: A dark feathered shadow runs inside the star along its upper and left edges (offset down-right), so the star looks recessed into the page, as the card says.

cards.name: Bitmap Pattern Transparency
cards.summary: Transparency type that uses a tiled bitmap image as the mask: the image's tones are read as grayscale and mapped between the Front and Back transparency values, so the object turns see-through in a photographic or grunge texture and whatever lies underneath shows through it. Applied with the Transparency tool's bitmap pattern type, or by script with an image file.
use_for: grunge / distressed texture knocked into a headline or logo
photo-textured shapes or type over a contrasting background
subtle paper or fabric texture on flat vector colour
avoid: crisp repeating geometric screens: Two-color Pattern Transparency gives hard-edged 1-bit patterns
when the picture itself should appear: use a bitmap pattern fill or PowerClip; transparency only modulates see-through
large high-resolution tiles: they bloat the file and slow printing
the harvest never applied this call (typelib only); which pattern is used without FileName is unverified

params.name: FileName
params.does: image file used as the pattern tile
params.typical: a grayscale grunge or paper texture

params.name: Front
params.does: transparency % given to one end of the image's tonal range

params.name: Back
params.does: transparency % given to the other end of the tonal range

params.name: TransformWithShape
params.does: pattern scales / rotates with the object when it is transformed
params.typical: true for logos that will be resized

pairs_with: heavy display type or solid badges, whose big fill areas show the texture
a contrasting background colour so the see-through areas read
Convert to Bitmap before export to bake the texture for print
cards.scripting: VBA: s.Transparency.ApplyPatternTransparency cdrBitmapPattern, "<PGD folder>\media\plate_photo.png", 1, 0, 100, False (Transparency.ApplyPatternTransparency(Type=2, FileName, PatternCanvasIndex, Front, Back, TransformWithShape) -> PatternFill). pywin32: s.Transparency.ApplyPatternTransparency(2, r"<PGD folder>\media\plate_photo.png", 1, 0, 100, False). Pass a native Windows path. Signature from the typelib only: not applied in the harvest.
cards.non_destructive: yes: transparency is a live object property; change its type and values or remove it at any time with the Transparency tool / property bar
cards.cost: moderate: the bitmap tile is stored and composited at redraw and print

review.changes: Front/Back: dropped the unharvested 0-100 range; otherwise none

verified.note: The star is see-through in the tones of the tiled photo: it shows a pale blue, photo-textured knockout (stripes, mid-tones and radial detail legible as light and dark) with the white page showing through, a photographic texture mask as described.

cards.name: Fountain Transparency
cards.summary: Graduated transparency: the object fades from the Start transparency to the End transparency along a linear, elliptical (radial), conical or rectangular (square) path, with angle, midpoint, edge pad, steps and centre-offset controls. It is the standard way to fade a shape, photo or type into the background or to make a mirror reflection fade out.
use_for: fade a photo or shape edge into the background
reflection under a product or logo that fades away
radial vignette or spotlight (elliptical type)
headline type that fades out over a busy background
avoid: an even see-through level: use Uniform Transparency
PS / EPS print workflows that flatten transparency into bands or bitmaps: export PDF and check
a soft edge all around a shape: a feathered shadow or a bitmap blur may read better than one fade
non-zero Steps if you want a smooth fade: steps can band it

params.name: Start
params.does: transparency % at the start node (0 = opaque, 100 = invisible)

params.name: End
params.does: transparency % at the end node
params.typical: 100 to vanish; 60-80 for a partial fade

params.name: Type
params.does: shape of the fade: linear, elliptical (radial), conical, rectangular (square)

params.name: Angle
params.does: direction of a linear fade, in degrees

params.name: Steps
params.does: number of bands in the fade; the default 0 keeps it smooth

params.name: EdgePad
params.does: how much of each end stays at the pure Start / End value before blending, %

params.name: MidPoint
params.does: where the halfway level falls between the nodes

params.name: CenterOffsetX
params.does: moves the centre of elliptical / conical / rectangular fades horizontally

params.name: CenterOffsetY
params.does: moves that centre vertically

pairs_with: a mirrored duplicate (reflection) with End 100 and Angle -90 / 90
Drop Shadow (Bottom) for a floor shadow plus reflection
PowerClip of a photo inside a shape that then fades
cards.scripting: VBA: s.Transparency.ApplyFountainTransparency 0, 100, cdrLinearFountainFill, 0, 0, 0, 50, 0, 0 (Transparency.ApplyFountainTransparency(Start, End, Type, Angle, Steps, EdgePad, MidPoint, CenterOffsetX, CenterOffsetY) -> FountainFill; harvest test: transparency_type 2). pywin32: s.Transparency.ApplyFountainTransparency(0, 100, 1, 0.0, 0, 0, 50, 0.0, 0.0).
cards.non_destructive: yes: transparency is a live object property; change its type and values or remove it at any time with the Transparency tool / property bar
cards.cost: light to edit; transparency may be flattened at PS / EPS export

verified.note: The star fades linearly from fully opaque blue at its left point to fully transparent at its right point (Start 0, End 100, linear).

cards.name: Texture Transparency
cards.summary: Transparency type that uses one of CorelDRAW's procedural bitmap textures from a texture library as the mask, mapping its tones between the Front and Back transparency values so the object turns see-through in an organic, mottled pattern. It needs a texture name (and usually its library); the preset harvest lists the libraries (Custom Data/texture.txr, library.txr) only as CorelDefaultID_<n> resource ids that the app resolves, so no usable name is known.
use_for: cloudy or smoky dissolve on shapes and type
organic mottled texture knocked into a flat background shape
weathered, stone-like see-through effect on a label
avoid: scripting without known names: TextureName (required) and LibraryName must be the resolved display names, not the CorelDefaultID_<n> ids in texture.txr / library.txr; read them from the Transparency tool's texture picker first
crisp repeating patterns: use Two-color or Vector Pattern Transparency
large objects at high texture resolution: heavy to render and print
the harvest never applied this call (typelib only)

cards.name: Two-color Pattern Transparency
cards.summary: Transparency type that uses a two-colour (1-bit) pattern tile such as dots, lines, checks or hatching as the mask: the pattern's foreground pixels take the Front transparency and its background pixels the Back transparency, giving a crisp screen- or stencil-like see-through pattern.
use_for: halftone-dot or line-screen look on a shape or type
retro striped or hatched see-through overlays
stencil-style pattern knockout for screen print or apparel graphics
avoid: soft or photographic textures: use Bitmap Pattern or Texture Transparency
very fine patterns printed small: they can moire or fill in
PatternCanvasIndex picks a pattern by its position in the installed list, which the harvest does not show; check which pattern you got
the harvest never applied this call (typelib only)

params.name: Back

params.does: pattern scales / rotates with the object when it is transformed
params.typical: true for artwork that will be resized

cards.name: Uniform Transparency
cards.summary: Applies one even transparency level to the whole object (Value 0 = opaque, 100 = invisible), so what lies underneath shows through uniformly: CorelDRAW's equivalent of an opacity slider, inverted (Value 60 is about 40% opacity). It stays live and editable from the Transparency tool or property bar.
use_for: tinted box behind text on a photo
ghosted watermark or background logo
overlapping semi-transparent shapes for colour-mix effects
knocking a colour block back so it does not compete with the headline
avoid: fading only part of an object: use Fountain Transparency
a lighter print tint of a spot colour: a tint value is safer than transparency (no flattening at output)
PS / EPS output over spot colours or overprints: transparency gets flattened; export PDF and check

params.name: Value
params.does: transparency in percent: 0 opaque, 100 fully transparent
params.typical: 20-40 subtle; 50-70 overlays and watermarks; 85+ faint ghost

pairs_with: a dark rectangle behind white type on a photo
white or light headline type set on top of the see-through box

cards.cost: light; transparency may be flattened at PS / EPS export
